paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The Spirit gives different gifts, but it's the same Spirit, the same Lord and the same God behind every one of them (1 Corinthians 12:4-6). Nobody gets skipped, because "to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good" (1 Corinthians 12:7). And the Spirit hands them out "as He determines," so you don't pick your gift off the shelf like a cookie cutter (1 Corinthians 12:11).

So where does that leave you? Paul says, "Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it" (1 Corinthians 12:27). If the foot says it doesn't belong because it isn't a hand, "that would not make it any less a part of the body" (1 Corinthians 12:15). God arranged every part "according to His design," so when you envy someone else's gift, you're arguing with the Designer, and I have tried that, friend, and I do NOT recommend it (1 Corinthians 12:18).

The other side matters just as much, because nobody is spare and nobody is the whole show: "The eye cannot say to the hand, 'I do not need you.'" (1 Corinthians 12:21). God gave greater honor to the parts that lacked it "so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another" (1 Corinthians 12:24-25). So whatever your gift is, use it for the body, and cheer loud when someone else's gift shines, because "if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it" (1 Corinthians 12:26). Paul's teaching isn't over, and he's about to show a most excellent way (1 Corinthians 12:31).
